script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The text does not say Leah stays in one place, is holding Reuben, or has a quick turnaround.
The contrast suggests Leah only turns to the LORD with Judah, though she also spoke of the LORD when Reuben and Simeon were born.
The text does not say there was a nursery or that it went quiet.
The text does not say the house got quieter after Leah stopped having children.
The text does not say Rachel speaks loudly.
The text says Rachel envied her sister, not that she was upset with her.
The explanation is flat and repetitive: it says Jacob names God rather than Leah twice, then adds an obvious detail about whom he addresses.
The text does not say whether Leah went to Rachel about this.
The text does not establish that Leah sent Jacob nowhere.
Leah says the women call her happy; the text does not establish that nobody calls her foolish.
The text does not say when Rachel heard about the mandrakes.
The text does not say Rachel comes along afterward.
The text does not say the exchange happens in a room or that the mandrakes are a handful.
Joseph is named in the same verse, not the verse before. The text also does not say Rachel is holding him.
